# Econ 101

### 1. Scarcity and Opportunity Cost 

The foundation of economics: resources are limited, so every choice has a cost — what you give up by not choosing the next best alternative.

**Opportunity cost of capital** — comparing returns:

```{r}

# You can invest $10,000 in Option A (5% return) or Option B (7% return)
option_a <- 10000 * 1.05
option_b <- 10000 * 1.07
opportunity_cost <- option_b - option_a
opportunity_cost 

```

### 2. Supply and Demand 

The demand curve slopes down (higher price -\> lower quantity demanded); supply curve slopes up.

#### The standard linear demand equation

$$Q_d = a-bP$$

Where $Q_d$ is the quantity demanded by consumers, $P$ is the price of the good or service, $a$ is the quantity intercept (total demand when the price is zero), and $b$ is the slope coefficient (how much the quantity demanded changes when the price changes)

#### The standard linear supply equation

$$Q_s = c + dP$$

Where $Q_s$ is the quantity supplied, $c$ is the intercept (the base quantity supplied when the price is zero), $d$ is the slope coefficient (the change in quantity supplied divided by the change in price ($\Delta Q / \Delta P$), and $P$ is the market price of the good or service.

```{r}

a <- 100; b <- 2
c <- 10; d <-3

price <- seq(0, 50, by=1)
Qd <- a - b*price
Qs <- c + d*price

eq_price <- (a-c) / (b+d)
eq_qty <- a - b * eq_price
cat("Equilibrium price:", eq_price, '\nEquilibrium quantity:', eq_qty)

```

```{r}
plot(price, Qd, type = "l", col = "blue", ylab = "Quantity", xlab = "Price",
     main = "Supply and Demand") 
lines(price, Qs, col='red')
abline(v=eq_price, lty=2)
legend("topright", legend = c("Demand", "Supply"), col = c("blue", "red"), lty = 1)
```

### 3. Elasticity 

Measures how responsive quantity is to price changes.

$$E_d = \frac{\%\Delta Q}{\%\Delta P}$$

```{r}
price_change_pct <- function(p1, p2) (p2 - p1) / p1
qty_change_pct   <- function(q1, q2) (q2 - q1) / q1

elasticity <- function(p1, p2, q1, q2) {
  qty_change_pct(q1, q2) / price_change_pct(p1, p2)
}

elasticity(10, 12, 100, 80)
```
